clue.text: Right to vote, having abandoned his country

indicators.note: what has been abandoned is left behind, so the following word drops out of the longer one

blocks.note: the franchise is the right to vote in elections
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: An emigrant gives up both his vote and his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HIS out of FRANCHISE and FRANC+E remains: FRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation in western Europe, an example of a country.

clue.text: Close friend's loud question about my veracity?

blocks.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
the question am I liar? doubts whether I tell the truth

explanation.surface: A close friend loudly asks whether I'm being honest.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun a familiar is an intimate companion, someone well known to you.

clue.text: Often how long a ruler is being prepared

blocks.note: taken as written
the length a standard school ruler usually measures is twelve inches
the measuring stick whose usual length is described

explanation.surface: A remark that rulers often measure a certain length, while something is underway.
explanation.walkthrough: A school ruler is usually twelve inches long, i.e. a foot; reading 'a ruler' as A + ruler's length gives A FOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans afoot are in preparation or under way.

clue.text: With no end in view, can talk, and in European language

indicators.note: with no end means each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who can talk endlessly in a European tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of can, talk and and loses its last letter: CA+TAL+AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalan is the Romance language spoken in Catalonia, in north-east Spain.

clue.text: Indian quickly protecting leader of Hindus

indicators.note: to protect something is to wrap round it, so one part encloses the other
'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Hindus'

blocks.note: apace is an old adverb for at speed
first letter of Hindus

explanation.surface: A swift bodyguard watches over a Hindu leader from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like it belongs to India with the Hindus, but it means a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, once commonly called American Indians.

clue.text: Current learner absorbed in head's system of exercises

indicators.note: what is absorbed in something is taken inside it

blocks.note: pate's, a head's, a pate being an old word for head
I is the symbol for electric current
L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A modern trainee is engrossed in the boss's workout regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is a noun here, the electrical kind, not an adjective meaning modern; pate is an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a method of body-conditioning exercise named after its inventor.

clue.text: Agreement producing new line in outerwear

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of pieces inside the garment word

blocks.note: a coat is worn outside other clothes
N is the abbreviation for new
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: A deal that launches a fresh range of coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' suggests a fashion range, but it is a length of string placed with N inside the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially one between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Sort of scan he or she can get ready for

indicators.note: a sort of version is a variant, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: the letters of scan and he

explanation.surface: A type of medical scan that a man or woman can prepare for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash (readies), so to get ready for something is to turn it into money; the words between fodder and definition just complete the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash a cheque or bond is to convert it into money, getting readies for it.

clue.text: No human is so sinful without guilt, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points at the very end, so only the closing letter of guilt is used
without in its old sense of outside, so the sinful word goes around the other piece

blocks.note: immoral means wicked or sinful
last letter of guilt

explanation.surface: A moral claim that no person is so sinful as to be free of guilt in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but here means outside: IMMOR(T)AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immortal never dies, so it cannot be a mortal human being.

clue.text: Money left — for example, change covering tip

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
e.g., for example
to alter is to change
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: Cash left over, with spare change for a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a gratuity and 'change' loose coins, but they mean an extremity and to modify.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is currency that must by law be accepted in payment of a debt.

clue.text: Lack of reason to revise any clue endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter of clue is cut
to revise is to rework, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
clue without its last letter

explanation.surface: Rewriting a crossword clue without end would be a madness of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is madness, the state of being without reason or sanity.

clue.text: Person intellectually challenged adding large number to 100

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a lot is a great many

explanation.surface: Someone poor at sums is trying to add a big figure to a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The large number is added after 100, so C comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid or clumsy person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Aid for maritime safety easily carried by legislative body

blocks.note: something light is easy to carry
a house of parliament, such as the Commons

explanation.surface: A safety measure for shipping passes through parliament with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easily carried' reads like a bill going through the House, but it means not heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse is a tower whose lamp warns ships away from rocks and guides navigation.

clue.text: Share deal is improperly justified

indicators.note: done improperly means done wrongly, so these letters fall out of their proper order

blocks.note: a ration is a fixed share
the letters of deal and is, rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy share deal is defended with excuses after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: To rationalise is to give plausible reasons for behaviour, so rationalised means explained away or excused.

clue.text: Became greater, as embraced by popular set of beliefs

indicators.note: what is embraced is held inside, so this word sits within the other

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a creed is a system of belief
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something grew as a popular faith took it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is not a link word here; it is taken literally and goes inside the beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Increased, the past tense of increase, means grew larger or became greater.

clue.text: Form of punishment one suffers as converted royalist

indicators.note: what is converted is changed into another form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters of royalist

explanation.surface: A royalist who changes sides is punished for turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary is short for solitary confinement, a prison punishment of being kept alone.

clue.text: Over a short time, change discussion

indicators.note: one thing laid over another covers it, so the longer word goes around the shorter

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
a conversion is a change from one form to another

explanation.surface: After a brief interval, the talk shifts to another subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as after, but it means the change word lies over, around, the short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is a talk between people, an informal discussion.

clue.text: New energy eclipsing old source of fossil fuel, as somebody proposed

indicators.note: to eclipse is to pass in front of and blot out, here taken as wrapping round

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
O is the abbreviation for old
coal comes from a mine
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Renewable power replacing the old coal pits is put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: N and E sit on either side of O+MINE: N(OMINE)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward as a candidate for a post or award.

clue.text: Join, in a way, including one enlisted man

indicators.note: what includes something holds it inside

blocks.note: to solder is one way of joining metal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up, with one recruit already in.
explanation.walkthrough: Joining metal with molten alloy is only one way to join, hence 'in a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a member of an army, especially a private rather than an officer.

clue.text: Saying nothing about application for place with collections

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
an application is a use

explanation.surface: Someone keeping quiet about their application for a job at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' suggests a job form, but it means putting something to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum is a building where collections of objects are kept and displayed.

clue.text: Top performer, in fashion, unusually pure? Seldom

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters take an unexpected arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of pure and seldom

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a leading fashion figure is often pure; seldom, comes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermodel is a highly paid, famous fashion model, the star of the catwalk.

clue.text: It may be up in the air pending 50/50 decision

definitions.text: It may be up in the air pending 50/50 decision

blocks.clueFragment: It may be up in the air pending 50/50 decision
blocks.note: surface reading: a matter still unresolved while a close decision hangs in the balance
setter's reading: literally flipped skyward before landing heads or tails, settling an even-chance choice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in the air' sounds like undecided, but it is meant literally: the thing is tossed to settle the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossing a piece of money gives heads or tails with even odds, a classic way to decide.

clue.text: They grow prickly about start of play

blocks.note: c, circa, means about
Act I is the opening of a play

explanation.surface: Players get irritable from the moment the show begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of play' tempts a single letter P, but it is the whole first act.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny desert plants, plants that grow covered in prickles.

clue.text: Body or soul

blocks.note: first meaning: an individual, as in 'a nice old body'
second meaning: a human being, as in 'not a soul in sight'

explanation.walkthrough: The clue poses as the old choice between body and soul, but both words name the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both body and soul are informal words for an individual human being.

clue.text: Artist at home applied layer of paint that's waterproof

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician
in means at home
a coat of paint

explanation.surface: A painter working at home lays on a coat of waterproof paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waterproof' looks like an adjective for the paint, but it is the noun for a rain garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof is a protective outer garment, the coat you wear against rain.

clue.text: Bizarre demand for incense

indicators.note: something bizarre is strange and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of demand

explanation.surface: An odd request for church incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' reads as the fragrant stuff burnt in church, but it is the verb meaning enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious, which is to madden them.

clue.text: Bright and breezy, initially, then wet

indicators.note: initially points at the start, so only the opening letter of breezy is used

blocks.note: first letter of breezy
rainy weather is wet

explanation.surface: A weather report: bright and breezy at first, rain later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' looks like part of the forecast, but it means clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright in the sense of intelligent; a brainy person is clever.
